reason: The flora says the fruit segments (méricarpes) are dehiscent. In Xylopia these are monocarps, the separate fruits from each carpel, not true mericarps (PO_0020075). So fruit with dehiscent (FLOPO_0991149) fits.
The bud is 4-6 x 2-2.8 mm. The first number is the length, 4-6 mm.
In Collenette, 'flowers N mm' gives the flower's width across. Diameter 9 mm is the usual reading.
In 'ovary 0.5–0.6 × ca. 0.3 mm' the second number is the width, about 0.3 mm. The 'ca.' could be kept as 'approximately', but the value is right.
'Flowers numerous' means flowers are present and many. That matches the count word.
The plant is 1–4 m tall in flower. Height with the flowering stage (PO_0007616) is right.

target: leaf lamina of the culm sheath (culm leaf)
fix: In bamboo descriptions, the words after 'Culm sheaths ...' (auricles, oral setae, ligule, blade) describe the sheath of the culm leaf. Its 'blade' is the culm-sheath blade, not the blade of the foliage leaves. Keep the culm sheath as the whole, or do not annotate it at taxon level as the leaf blade.
reason: 'Blade reflexed, tiny, narrow' belongs to the culm-sheath description that comes before 'Leaf sheaths ...'. As written, the annotation says the leaf blades are tiny, which is false for the foliage leaves.

fix: With 'Fronds strongly dimorphic. Sterile fronds ..., lamina ...' the sizes belong to the sterile frond only. Keep the sterile or fertile state of the frond. Fertile fronds are described separately and differ.
reason: The 1-7 cm is the length of the sterile frond blade only. In this species the fertile fronds are longer, so the annotation without that state is false for the plant.
The single leaf is ovate or oblong. Those two alternatives on the leaf blade are right, and FLOPO_0991024 is the stand-in class for ovate.
The pinnae are sessile.
'Graines ... à caroncule' means the seeds have a caruncle, so caruncle present is right.

target: leaf (PO_0025034), probably; the noun after 'with' is cut off
fix: In 'A ... herb ... with <colour> <adjective> [noun]', the colour belongs to the noun after 'with', not to the whole plant. If that noun is missing from the text, do not annotate. Also, 'blue-green glaucous' is not just green: use the value class 'glaucous blue-green' (FLOPO_0980182) and do not mark it as approximate.
reason: The plant is called 'green' on its own. 'Blue-green glaucous' describes some part named after 'with', most likely the leaves, and the text is cut off.
The filaments are adnate to the perianth segments, and the 'towards' slot names the perianth segments.

target: position: abaxial surface of the leaf lamina
fix: 'surfaces abaxially X' (or 'abaxial surface X') must keep the abaxial position. Without it, the hairiness is said of the whole blade.
reason: Only the lower (abaxial) surface is said to be glabrous or hispid. The upper surface is not described, so 'lamina glabrous or hispid' says more than the flora does.
The bracts are 1-1.6 × 0.8-1 mm. The first number is the length, 1-1.6 mm.

The adaxial nectary is oblong, square or ovate. The 'staminate flowers' and adaxial settings are not kept, but in this species the pistillate nectaries have the same shapes, so the statement is still true.
The sepals reflex at anthesis. The flowering stage covers anthesis.
'Petals ... apex rounded, emarginate, or parted' is a list of alternatives. Emarginate petal apex is one of them, and the part is the petal apex.

fix: For '<Part> ... veinless', the absence of veins needs the named part as the container: vascular bundle absent, part of the perigynium. Without the container it says the whole plant has no veins.
reason: Only the perigynia are veinless. As written, the annotation says the plant has no vascular bundles, which is false.
The free hyaline ligule is (3–)5–15 mm long. The main range 5–15 and the extreme low value 3 are right.
The pedicels are 3-8 mm long in fruit. Using the fruit development stage for that is right.
The female flowers have 3 styles. The female-flower setting is not kept, but only female flowers have styles here.

target: paleaceous: made of scales (a pappus structure), not the texture 'scarious'; whole = outer pappus series
fix: French 'paléacé' or English 'paleaceous' said of a pappus means 'made of paleae (scales)', so it describes the pappus's make-up, not its texture. Do not map it to scarious (FLOPO_0991047). Also, 'pappus double, l'externe X, l'interne Y' assigns X to the outer series only.
reason: The outer pappus is made of scales and the inner of bristles. The flora does not say the pappus is thin, dry and membranous, and it does not describe the whole pappus as one thing.
The leaf base is usually rounded. PATO obtuse (PATO_0001935) has the synonym 'roundish', and there is no separate FLOPO class for 'rounded'. The part and the 'usually' are right.
The blade is 3(-5)-veined: 3 veins, rarely up to 5, with the leaf blade as the container. Floating leaves are absent, so all leaves are submerged.
There are 2 secondary veins on each side of the midvein. The 'each side' position and the midvein landmark are kept.
The floral tube (hypanthium) is glandular-pubescent.

fix: In '<part> ..., apex X or Y', the shape belongs to the apex. Here the apex word was read as part of the value text ('apex obtuse') instead of setting the part. It should replace the part with its apex, as the place-on-part rule does elsewhere.
reason: The tip of the calyx lobes is obtuse or slightly acute. The sepal as a whole is ovate.
The leaf blade is brownish when dry. Brown, marked as approximate, with the dried-specimen condition is right.
The margin of the inner phyllaries is narrowly scarious. Phyllaries are bracts, so bract margin plus scarious is true. The 'inner' setting is not kept, but this does not make it false.
